chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Holding the sticks; subbing in the pit and seeing his name on the screen
summary: Bonomo had shown him the grip; at the theatre Abner Jones increasingly left him in the pit, and one day the screen billed him as Abner Jones' protege.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: I mean, did you know anything about how to hold your sticks?
Oh, yes, oh, yes, I learned that in Beaumont, see.
Oh, yeah, that's right.
And Mr. Bonomo was his name.
Yes, he showed --
Joe Bonomo was his name.
Yeah.
And he showed me how to hold the sticks and everything.
Yeah.
Well, I was holding the sticks like
that before I even came there, because I was beating on the chairs.
And you just lucked up to do the right thing. Is that right?
That's right.
That's what you call a natural drummer.
And so by being in Houston and playing in the pit, anytime I would come to the theatre, he would get up and leave, just to go out and talk to somebody he knew.
That suited him.
Sure.
And nobody in the band had anything to say?
As long as I kept good time, they didn't mind.
They didn't mind.
No.
And you didn't try to do anything too fancy.
Oh, no, no. All I wanted to do was play right along with them.
That's right. You had the good sense not to want to be cute.
That's right.
You weren't a bigmouth or anything.
No, no.
Yeah, no, no, nothing flashy.
Nothing flashy. And one day, they showed me playing -- they flashed it on the screen. Abner Jones' protege.
Really?
Yes, in the theatre. Oh, that was really --
With your name?
With my name.
That was the first time you saw your name up.
